transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, hi. Thank you. I came in because I just feel... wound up almost all day long. It’s like my body is constantly bracing for something. Even when I’m just sitting at my computer for work. I do a lot of data processing, and they actually just forced us to switch to this new software system last week. It has been a complete mess, honestly. Half the office couldn't even get their accounts to migrate properly, and my coworker Dave was on hold with the help desk for three hours on Tuesday. 

But anyway, even when I'm just sitting there at my desk, or trying to relax after dinner—I've been trying out these new sheet-pan recipes, which are supposed to be easy but honestly there's still so much chopping involved, especially with butternut squash, which is nearly impossible to cut—I just feel completely braced and tense. I just can't seem to unwind.
Do you find that you worry a lot about different things in your life, even when there isn’t an obvious problem, or has this tension been mostly about work and the software change lately?

Oh, no, it’s definitely not just the software. I mean, that certainly doesn't help, but my mind just keeps going from one concern to another all day long. I'll be thinking about whether I missed something at the office, and then suddenly I’m worrying about my sister down in Arecibo. She’s been living in Puerto Rico for, gosh, almost twelve years now. It's beautiful over there, but the humidity is just terrible, and she was telling me on Sunday about this new dehumidifier she bought that sounds like a jet engine in her living room. I told her she should just take it back to the store, but she lost the receipt, which is just so typical of her... 

But anyway, yes, I worry about her. And then my brain just jumps right to my husband driving home from work—people drive like absolute maniacs on the interstate lately, especially with that construction on I-95—or I'm stressing over my church commitments for the weekend, or if the bills are paid on time. I just find myself constantly preparing for problems that haven’t even happened yet. It's like I'm always waiting for the other shoe to drop, even when everything is technically fine.
Do you find yourself feeling restless or unable to relax, even when you’re not actively worrying about something?

Well, yes, exactly. Like I was saying earlier, I just feel wound up almost all day long. It's like my body is constantly bracing for something, even when I'm not actively thinking about the software or my sister or anything else. Even when I'm just sitting at my computer, or trying to relax after dinner. Speaking of dinner, my husband actually brought home takeout last night from that new Thai place on 4th Street because I was just too exhausted to deal with the butternut squash again. Have you been there? The Pad Thai was okay, but they use those really flimsy plastic containers, and the sauce leaked all over the passenger seat of his car. He was so upset about it because he just got it detailed last month for our anniversary. We went up to the mountains for our anniversary, actually, which was supposed to be relaxing, but... anyway, yes, even when I'm just sitting there, not worrying about a specific thing, I just feel completely braced and tense. I can't seem to just sit still and unwind.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, shaking, or feeling short of breath when you're feeling this tension or worry?

No, I don't really get any of those things. No racing heart or sweating or anything like that. It's really just that constant tension in my muscles, like I'm clenching up. My shoulders are always so tight, which is probably why I've been getting these headaches. I thought maybe I needed a new pillow, so I ordered one of those memory foam ones off the internet. It took two weeks to get here because the mail has just been so slow lately. Our regular carrier, Stan, retired back in October, and the new guy they put on our route keeps mixing up our mail with the Johnsons down the street. They live at 412 and we're 421, so I guess I can see how it happens, but it's just so frustrating. Anyway, the pillow didn't even help. But no, I don't get the sweating or the shortness of breath. Just the muscle tension.
Do you feel like you have trouble controlling your worry, even when you try to stop or shift your thoughts?

Yes, it's incredibly hard to stop it once it starts. I'll be sitting at my desk, and I’ll tell myself, 'Daniela, enough, just focus on this report,' but it never works. One small thought pops in, and then that turns into five more, and before I know it, I’ve spent half an hour checking my messages or just sitting there replaying everything that could possibly go wrong. It reminds me of how my mother used to be. She was always worrying about something, mostly about whether she left the stove on. We lived in this older house in Chicago, and the stove was gas, one of those big heavy vintage ones. They don't make appliances like that anymore, do they? Now everything is digital and breaks after three years. We had to replace our refrigerator last spring because the ice maker just completely gave out, and the repairman said it would cost more to fix the computer board than to just buy a new one. Can you believe that? A perfectly good refrigerator going to the landfill just because of one little computer chip. But yes, the worry just spirals, and trying to stop it feels almost impossible.
Have these feelings of constant tension and worry been happening even during times when things are going smoothly in your life, or do they mostly come up when something specific is going on?

Well, that's the thing, it really doesn't seem to matter if things are going smoothly or not. Even when everything is perfectly fine, I still feel it. Like, last month, we finally finished the landscaping in the backyard. We had this big dead oak tree taken down, which was a whole ordeal because the tree service had to bring in a crane. They had to park it right on the street, and I was so worried it was going to block the mail truck—not that Stan is our mailman anymore, but still. Anyway, the yard looks beautiful now. We planted all these hydrangeas, the blue ones, which my husband says need special acidic soil, so he bought all this fertilizer. He's been out there every weekend fussing over them. He even bought this special watering can from a catalog. It's copper, very heavy. I don't know why anyone would want a heavy watering can, honestly, my wrists ache just looking at it. But anyway, yes, even sitting on the patio, looking at the nice new yard, with absolutely nothing going wrong, I just... I still feel that tension. It just doesn't go away.

Have these feelings of constant tension and worry significantly affected your ability to function in your daily life, such as making it harder to do your job, be with family, or enjoy your usual activities?

Well, I suppose I'm still getting everything done, you know? I still go to work, I still show up for family dinners, and I haven't missed a Sunday at church. Oh, our church just got a new pastor, actually. Pastor Miller retired after twenty years—such a lovely man, his wife made the best potato salad for the church picnics. The new pastor is very young, he wears jeans to the service sometimes, which took some getting used to for the older congregation. He brought in a guitar player for the choir, too. My husband says it's good to modernize, but I just don't know if a guitar belongs next to the organ. The organ we have is from the 1920s, it has these beautiful brass pipes... but anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, my daily life. I'm still functioning, but it just takes a toll. Like at work, it takes me so much longer to finish my reports now because I'm constantly double-checking everything. I'll read the same paragraph three times just to be sure I didn't miss a comma. And I've noticed I can be a bit... snappy. I've had to apologize a few times for sounding short with my husband and my sister, which isn't like me. I just feel so wound up all the time.
How long have you been feeling this way, with constant tension and worry most of the day, nearly every day?

Well, I've been keeping track, and it's been about thirteen months. It really started right around the time my sister in Arecibo began needing much more help from the family. Arecibo is in Puerto Rico, you know, right on the northern coast. It used to be so wonderful to visit her there, even though the humidity is just terrible for my hair. Did you know they had that giant radio telescope there? The one that collapsed a few years ago? My husband was just devastated when that happened, he's always loved astronomy. He actually has this massive telescope set up in our guest bedroom right now, the room facing the street. Which is just silly, honestly, because the streetlights are so bright you can't see a single star. I keep telling him he needs to pack it up and take it out to the country if he actually wants to use it, but he says the tripod is too heavy to keep moving around in the trunk of the car. He bought it second-hand from a retired science teacher who was moving into a condo... wait, I'm sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, how long I've been feeling this way. Yes, about thirteen months, ever since my sister started needing the extra help.
